patterns.name: Strung out
patterns.text: Small, equal shot spaced evenly through the bottom of the rig. Slow, natural fall — best in shallow water or when fish feed on the drop.

patterns.name: Bulk & droppers
patterns.text: Most of the weight bunched part-way down, with two or three small droppers below. Gets the bait down quickly past small fish and holds steady in deeper water.

patterns.name: Olivette
patterns.text: A single streamlined pole weight in place of the bulk. The most stable choice for heavier pole floats in deep water, wind or tow.

patterns.name: Shirt button
patterns.text: Equal shot spaced evenly from float to hook on a stick float. The classic pattern for steady running water.

patterns.name: Locking + droppers
patterns.text: Waggler weight locked either side of the float for casting, with a few small shot down the line to cock the float and show bites.

patterns.name: Slider
patterns.text: A big waggler (4AAA and up) that runs on the line, with a bulk of shot or an olivette below it and a stop knot above setting the depth. The way to float fish water deeper than your rod is long.

patterns.name: Loaded waggler
patterns.text: Weight is already in the base, so silicone float stops set the depth instead of locking shot. Most of the shot printed after the plus sits around the adaptor, with a few No.8 droppers down the line. The same weight can go on as 2BB, No.4 or No.6 with nothing down the line.

patterns.name: Pellet waggler
patterns.text: All weight at the float so the pellet falls slowly alongside the feed. Many are pre-loaded.
